metadata.name: fg
metadata.displayName: fg - Bring a job to the foreground
metadata.description: Move a background or stopped job to the foreground

installation.note: fg is a shell built-in (commonly in bash), not a standalone binary

overview.summary: The fg command brings a job to the foreground, attaching it to your terminal so you can interact with it. It's used with job control, typically alongside Ctrl+Z, bg, and jobs.
when_to_use: Bring a background job back to the terminal to interact with it
Resume a stopped job in the foreground
Manage multiple jobs in a single terminal session

syntax.description: If JOB_SPEC is omitted, fg operates on the current job. JOB_SPEC is often like %1, %2, etc., shown by the jobs command.

examples.title: Bring the most recent job to the foreground
examples.description: Resume the current job in the foreground
examples.use_case: Return to an interactive program you backgrounded or stopped

examples.title: Bring a specific job to the foreground
examples.description: Bring job number 1 to the foreground
examples.use_case: When multiple jobs exist and you need a specific one

common_pitfalls.issue: Using fg in the wrong shell
common_pitfalls.description: fg only affects jobs in the current shell session; it can't control processes started elsewhere.
common_pitfalls.solution: Run jobs to confirm the job exists in the current shell, or use tools like ps/kill for general process control.

related_commands.description: Resume a stopped job in the background
List jobs to find job numbers for fg/bg
Send signals to processes (not job-spec specific unless used through the shell)
